ds: Restricted goods or restricted-destination trade may be rerouted through third countries whose trade statistics, parties or documents show sudden shifts. Financial institutions can detect diversion by comparing customer activity with country-level trade patterns, end-use information and common high-priority items.

ind.n: Customer in transit country suddenly trades controlled or high-priority items
ind.cx: A firm with a different history begins importing restricted items for resale.
ind.fp: Market expansion and new product lines occur.

ind.n: Orders from addresses in transit zones with no storage or sales operations
ind.cx: Items ordered and shipped to mailbox or warehouse addresses without a visible business.
ind.ds: Goods or cards are shipped to freight forwarders, reshippers, mail drops or addresses with no storage or sales operations or link to the buyer.
ind.cn: Delivery to forwarder, mailbox or address unrelated to buyer

ind.ds: Customer or buyer is evasive about end use, final destination or end-user certificate, or declines re-export undertakings.
ind.cn: End-user information vague, missing or refused

ind.cx: Aggregate trade data shows spikes in categories of concern to particular countries.
ind.ds: Aggregate trade data shows spikes in categories of concern to particular countries.

ind.cx: Funds arrive from or return to parties in the restricted jurisdiction.
ind.ds: Funds arrive from or return to parties in the restricted jurisdiction.

ind.ds: Descriptions change between stages of the supply chain.

ctl.ds: Screens goods descriptions, HS codes and items against export-control, precursor and procurement watch lists, with access to technical review. It catches proliferation-sensitive and restricted goods.

ctl.n: Counterparty capacity and trade profile assessment
ctl.ds: Tests whether a counterparty's size, history, equipment and sector make the traded volume and goods plausible, and models an expected trade profile to alert on deviation. It detects trading that is out of line with the business.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.

Validates a stated address against postal or reference data, requires recent independent proof of residence or premises, and flags known mass-registration or virtual-office addresses. It supports identity assurance and helps reveal fictitious or shared addresses.

Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.
Obtains contractual and documentary undertakings restricting re-export or onward sale to specified destinations and flags rapid resale patterns. It limits diversion of goods to prohibited end users.

ctl.n: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
ctl.ds: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.

Compares reported volumes with capacity, production, mass balance, concession size and national trade statistics to test whether quantities are physically possible. It exposes inflated, laundered or mislabelled flows.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.

ctl.n: Scenario tuning and independent model validation
ctl.ds: Periodically tests thresholds, coverage and segmentation, including above and below the line, and independently validates scenarios and models with documented rationale for changes. It keeps detection effective and defensible.
